Revised narrative:

---

The differential metabolite list is dominated by eicosanoids and their direct precursors, and the RaMP enrichment confirms this with overwhelming statistical force. **Eicosanoid synthesis** (WikiPathways WP167) is the top hit, with an FDR of 0.0 and a fold-enrichment of 1,111.9 — five of the nine input metabolites map to this pathway (arachidonic acid C00219, leukotriene A4 C00909, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ C14717, 5-HETE C04805, and 15-HETE C04742). Two secondary SMPDB pathways also score as top hits with identical matched compounds: the **Rofecoxib Action Pathway** (SMP00087) and **Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency** (SMP00353), both consistent with compounds that interface with the arachidonic acid cascade.

**Key drivers.** Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the canonical entry point. KEGG graph traversal confirms it is upstream of leukotriene A4 (C00909) via the two-hop route C00219 → C05356 (5-HPETE) → C00909, placing it as a master precursor. Arachidonic acid is also confirmed as a precursor of 5-HETE (C04805) along the 5-lipoxygenase branch, and of 15-HETE (C04742) along the 15-lipoxygenase branch. Thiosulfate (C05529) and xanthine (C00385) did not match the top-ranked pathways and may represent independent treatment effects.

**Biological significance.** Coordinated elevation of arachidonic acid together with its downstream eicosanoids — leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, and the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ — points to strong engagement of the **Eicosanoid synthesis** pathway, activating both the cyclooxygenase (COX) and lipoxygenase (LOX) arms of the arachidonic acid cascade. Elevated 5-HETE and leukotriene A4 are consistent with pro-inflammatory signaling (supported by literature: PMID 41901114, 41901287), while 15-HETE and 15-deoxy-PGJ₂ are associated with anti-inflammatory and pro-resolving activity. The androgen precursor 5-androstenediol (C04295) is also present, which may reflect cross-talk between steroid metabolism and inflammatory resolution. Methylmalonic acid (C02170), a propionate catabolite, does not cluster with the eicosanoid module and may indicate a secondary metabolic disturbance.

**Limitations.** The two metabolites that did not match the top eicosanoid pathways (thiosulfate C05529, xanthine C00385) could not be contextualized using the returned pathway rankings alone; their biological roles in this study would require additional database queries or literature support.
